messages:
noa: Kicking off onboarding thread for cust-tethys LoRA merge onto oak-13b-v2.1. Quick-eval shows token aliasing for currency + a measurable int4 drop. Keeping notes here.
rita: Short TL;DR?
noa: Their package: adapter ~95MB, tokenizer.json adds two specials (<TXN_ID>, <CURRENCY_USD>) and remaps a contiguous block of ~12 ids in the 2400-2412 range. When we splice weights naively, a few punctuation/currency symbols get split into two tokens.
sam: Did you hit any runtime issues?
noa: One streaming error on multi-tenant tests:
```
RuntimeError: kv_cache offset mismatch: expected slots=20 got=16
  at runtime/kv_cache.cc:172
```
Root cause was model.config.max_position_embeddings left at 4096 while we replayed 7000-token sequences. Locally bumped to 8192 and streaming stabilized. Also discovered that our KV layout code assumed token id continuity for some edge cases; added a guard.
lee: Numbers from quick-eval (invoice extraction, 500-sample pack):
- oak-13b-v2.1 fp16 (baseline): exact_match=0.84 f1=0.92
- tethys-lora merged fp16: exact_match=0.82 f1=0.90
- tethys-lora merged int4 (per-channel asym): exact_match=0.79 f1=0.88
So int4 accounts for most of the delta here (~0.03 EM vs fp16 merge). There's an extra ~0.01 EM gap from tokenizer detokenize diffs.
rita: Can you paste a minimal failing example?
noa: Example minimal: 
```
input: "Invoice total: $4,500.00"
baseline: "Total: $4,500.00"
merged-fp16: "Total: $4,500.00"
merged-int4: "Total 4500.00 dollars"
```
Observed that the $ token became a two-token sequence in the candidate tokenization.
sam: Run token diff and post the mapping snippet.
noa: token_diff snippet: `$ => base:[2507] candidate:[241,3920] ; "," => base:[45] candidate:[45]` Occurs ~0.28% of samples in the quickpack (above our 0.1% preflight threshold).
lee: Two remediation approaches: A) reindex LoRA to base tokenizer ids (accurate but needs weight re-save + verification), B) lightweight runtime remap layer that collapses known split sequences back to logical symbols during detokenize/eval.
rita: Any quant sims or QAT runs?
noa: Ran quick quant_sim (per-channel asymmetric) and a 400-step QAT sim on LoRA only. eval-bot posted artifacts.
eval-bot: quant_sim summary uploaded: /artifacts/tethys/1798801234/quant_sim.json. Per-channel int4 projected EM delta = -0.04 vs merged-fp16. QAT (400 steps) projects EM delta = -0.015. Full logs in artifact bundle.
sam: Good. Short-term rollout plan?
lee: Propose canary the merged-fp16 variant at 3% on a dedicated pool while we stabilize int4. For int4, either require QAT or token-aligned remerge showing EM within 0.02 of fp16 before any user traffic. Add a fallback policy: if sliding EM_drop >= 0.035 over 1k requests revert.
rita: Also add an automated token-drift check into quick-eval CI: flag any base token that maps to >1 tokens in candidate for >0.1% samples and block auto-rollout. I'll add the rule.
noa: Implemented a small preprocess remap that collapses [241,3920] -> "$" for evaluation and production preflight. Reran int4 quickpack: exact_match improved 0.79 -> 0.805. Better but still shy of fp16-merged. Recorded diffs and examples in the onboard ticket.
sam: File a ticket and link artifacts. Then we can prioritize either QAT or a remerge path.
noa: Ticket created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/customer-onboards/issues/4477 with token dumps, token_diff output, failing samples, and suggested fixes.
deploy-bot: Canary requested: tethys-lora-fp16 -> dedicated/pool-14 (3%). Fallback configured: revert on EM_drop >= 0.035 sliding window 1k requests.
lee: Action items: (1) no a/rita: expand preprocess remap to other known splits and produce final eval artifacts, (2) sam: run token-aligned remerge experiment and longer QAT run (1k steps) on LoRA params, (3) rita: add token-drift preflight rule & CI alert, (4) deploy-bot/ops: monitor canary dashboards and trigger fallback if needed.
noa: We'll hold int4 rollout until we have QAT or remerge artifacts that predict EM within 0.02 of fp16. Reopen when artifacts are ready. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
